description: A classic oscillator whose wave moves smoothly from triangle through saw to square, with the aliasing suppressed

params.text: Sets the pitch, -4 to 4 as a power of two around middle C, which is about 16Hz to 4186Hz
Scales the voltage at the FM jack, 0 to 300 per cent
While on, the FM jack is added to the frequency in hertz rather than to the pitch in octaves, which gives through-zero frequency modulation
Sets the wave, 0 to 1: a triangle at 0, a saw at 0.3, a square at 0.6, and from 0.6 upward a square whose width narrows
Attenuates the voltage at the Wave CV jack before it is added to the Wave knob, 0 to 100 per cent
While on, a sync signal nudges the phase rather than forcing it back to the start, which is softer

inputs.text: Sets the pitch by cable, 1V per octave added to the knob, one channel per voice
Modulates the frequency through the FM knob; with Lin off it is added to the pitch in octaves, and with Lin on it is added to the frequency itself, which lets it pass through zero
Modulates the wave, a tenth per volt scaled by the Wave CV knob
Forces the phase back to the start of the cycle when the voltage here rises, one channel per voice

outputs.text: The wave, -5V to 5V, with its constant offset removed

notes: the wave is worked out sixteen times over per sample and filtered, which keeps the square and saw settings from aliasing
the Wave CV jack is read on one channel only, so every voice gets the same wave shape

inputs.1:
bipolar · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.2:
continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
